description: Semantic specification for the simple Producer-Consumer Akka benchmark. The cross-language contract focuses on payload-preserving message transformation, FIFO order, exact delivery count, topology, and terminal quiescence.
evaluation_principle: Evaluate the observable Produce(item) -> Consume(item) protocol on one connected RMC execution path. Logging/println is outside the cross-language contract. Payload identities may use a behavior-preserving symbolic encoding.

payload_encoding.requirement: Whatever target representation is used, the payload consumed by Produce must be exactly the payload forwarded in the corresponding Consume.

tests.description: Produce(item1) consumes exactly one input and enqueues exactly one Consume(item1) for Consumer.
Produce(item2) consumes exactly one input and enqueues exactly one Consume(item2) for Consumer.
One connected state-graph execution forwards both startup items without loss.
For each benchmark message, the Consume payload is identical to the corresponding Produce payload.
The logical forwarding order is item1 followed by item2.
Producer and Consumer rebecs exist; behavior-preserving auxiliary rebecs are allowed.
Both startup Produce requests execute on one connected path.
Startup produces exactly the logical Consume sequence [item1, item2], one output per Produce.
After exactly two Consumer Consume transitions, the system reaches a terminal state with all rebec queues empty.

out_of_scope: source-only stress scenarios without a target test harness
